arxiv-2203-01717.title: Practitioner Motives to Use Different Hyperparameter Optimization Methods DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Journal: TOCHI Volume: 37 4 111 8 CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in HCI CCS: Human-centered computing HCI theory, concepts and models CCS: Human-centered computing User models
arxiv-2203-01717.creator: Niclas Kannengießer, Niklas Hasebrook, Felix Morsbach, Marc-André Zöller, Jörg K.H. Franke, Marius Lindauer, Frank Hutter, Ali Sunyaev
arxiv-2203-01717.description: Abstract . Programmatic hyperparameter optimization (HPO) methods, such as Bayesian optimization and evolutionary algorithms, are highly sample-efficient in identifying optimal hyperparameter configurations for machine learning (ML) models. However, practitioners frequently use less efficient methods, such as grid search, which can lead to under-optimized models. We suspect this behavior is driven by a range of practitioner-specific motives.

arxiv-2206-12925.creator: Hua-Bao Ling, Bowen Zhu, Dong Huang, Ding-Hua Chen
arxiv-2206-12925.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Hua-Bao Ling, Bowen Zhu, Dong Huang, Ding-Hua Chen. Vision Transformer (ViT) has shown its advantages over the convolutional neural network (CNN) with its ability to capture global long-range dependencies for visual representation learning. Besides ViT, contrastive learning is another popular research topic recently. While previous contrastive learning works are mostly based on CNNs, some recent studies have attempted to combine ViT and contrastive learning for enhanced self-supervised learning.

arxiv-2304-08824.title: A Dark Matter Probe in Accreting Pulsar-Black Hole Binaries
arxiv-2304-08824.creator: Ali Akil, Qianhang Ding
arxiv-2304-08824.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ali Akil, Qianhang Ding. The accretion of dark matter (DM) into astrophysical black holes slowly increases their mass. The rate of this mass accretion depends on the DM model and the model parameters. If this mass accretion effect can be measured accurately enough, it is possible to rule out some DM models, and, with the sufficient technology and the help of other DM constraints, possibly confirm one model.

arxiv-2308-12122.creator: Fábio L. Braghin, Marcelo Loewe, Cristian Villavicencio
arxiv-2308-12122.description: Abstract Weak magnetic field induced corrections for the Yukawa potential due to one pion exchange between two constituent quarks (nucleons) are presented. For that, the constant magnetic field effect on the pion propagator and on the pion form factor are taken into account. An effective gluon propagator parameterized with an effective gluon mass ( M g ∼ 0.5 M_{g}\sim 0.

arxiv-2309-05978.title: CToMP: A Cycle-task-oriented Memory Protection Scheme for Unmanned Systems
arxiv-2309-05978.creator: Chengyan MA, Ning XI, Di LU, Yebo FENG, Jianfeng MA
arxiv-2309-05978.description: Abstract Memory corruption attacks (MCAs) refer to malicious behaviors of system intruders that modify the contents of a memory location to disrupt the normal operation of computing systems, causing leakage of sensitive data or perturbations to ongoing processes. Unlike general-purpose systems, unmanned systems cannot deploy complete security protection schemes, due to their limitations in size, cost and performance.

arxiv-2310-05895.title: Spatial asymmetry of optically excited spin waves in anisotropic ferromagnetic film
arxiv-2310-05895.creator: N. E. Khokhlov, Ia. A. Filatov, A. M. Kalashnikova
arxiv-2310-05895.description: Abstract We analytically discuss and micromagnetically prove the ways to tune the spatial asymmetry of the initial phase, amplitude, and wavevectors of magnetostatic waves driven by ultrafast laser excitation. We consider that the optical pulse heats a thin ferromagnetic metallic film and abruptly decreases the saturation magnetization and the parameter of uniaxial anisotropy.

arxiv-2311-08040.title: On the Masking-Friendly Designs for Post-Quantum Cryptography
arxiv-2311-08040.creator: Suparna Kundu, Angshuman Karmakar, Ingrid Verbauwhede
arxiv-2311-08040.description: Abstract Masking is a well-known and provably secure countermeasure against side-channel attacks. However, due to additional redundant computations, integrating masking schemes is expensive in terms of performance. The performance overhead of integrating masking countermeasures is heavily influenced by the design choices of a cryptographic algorithm and is often not considered during the design phase.

arxiv-2409-01429.title: Investigating the Impact of Qubit Velocity on Quantum Synchronization Dynamics
arxiv-2409-01429.creator: Amir Hossein Houshmand Almani, Alireza Nourmandipour, Ali Mortezapour
arxiv-2409-01429.description: Abstract We investigate the quantum synchronization dynamics of a moving qubit interacting with a dissipative cavity environment, using the Husimi Q Q -function to analyze its phase space evolution. Unlike conventional synchronization between separate subsystems, we focus on self-synchronization phenomena, where the qubit’s phase dynamics exhibit locking to its initial phase distribution.

arxiv-2502-03832.title: Correlated helimagnetic configuration in a nonsymmorphic magnetic nodal semimetal
arxiv-2502-03832.creator: Xi Luo 1, Yu-Ge Chen 2, Ye-Min Zhan 3, Yue Yu 3
arxiv-2502-03832.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xi Luo 1, Yu-Ge Chen 2, Ye-Min Zhan 3, Yue Yu 3. Nonsymmorphic magnetic Weyl semimetal materials such as ReAlX (Re=rare earth, X=Si/Ge) provide a unique opportunity to explore the correlated phenomena between Weyl fermions and nontrivial magnetic configurations. To be specific, we study a lattice model in which the magnetic configuration is determined by the competition among ferromagnetic (FM) interaction, the Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interaction, and the Kondo coupling K 0 K_{0} to the Weyl fermion.

pmc-10628306.creator: Wenfei Liu, Li Zhang, Liwen He, Hailang Liu
pmc-10628306.description: In fatigue data analysis, fitting accurate P-S-N curve is problematic if only a small number of specimen is available, especially to evaluate the relationship between the stress level and the standard deviation. This paper proposes a sample information reconstruction method that can effectively solve this problem.

pmc-10648704.title: Higher Risk of Reoperation after Total Knee Arthroplasty in Young and Elderly Patients
pmc-10648704.creator: Albert T Anastasio, Billy I Kim, Niall H Cochrane, Elshaday Belay, Michael P Bolognesi, Grayson M Talaski, Sean P Ryan, Bongju Kim
pmc-10648704.description: As outcomes and survivorship improve, total knee arthroplasty (TKA) has expanded into broader age groups. The purpose of this study is to analyze the impact of age on TKA outcomes using the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (NSQIP) database from 2015 to 2020. Patients were categorized into young (40–49 years), middle (50–79 years), and elderly (80–89 years) groups.

pmc-11690195.title: CULTIVATING BELONGINGNESS: IN TEMPORARY SUPPORTIVE HOUSING FOR OLDER MALE VETERANS IN CALGARY, CANADA
pmc-11690195.creator: Christine Walsh
pmc-11690195.description: Veterans are two to three times more likely to experience homelessness compared to the general population, with an estimated 2,400 – 10,000+ homeless veterans in Canada. Veterans tend to be older, male, and more likely to cite an illness or medical condition as a contributing factor to their homelessness, than their non-veteran counterparts and thus have distinctly different needs.

pmc-13547862.title: Attentional modulation of contamination sensitivity: sharper perceptual boundaries for food compared to nonfood odor mixtures
pmc-13547862.creator: Leonie Seidel, Astrid Endrup Iversen, Konstantina Kilteni, Janina Seubert
pmc-13547862.description: Processing of contaminants in odor mixtures is influenced by their categorization into food and nonfood categories. For example, we previously found that participants were more likely to perceive food odors as contaminated by nonfood odors than vice versa, and that this effect was robust to changes in explicit task instructions.

pmc-13661522.title: Tubular tRF‑1:30‑Gln‑CTG‑4 attenuates tubulointerstitial fibrosis by mitigating FBXO7-mediated mitophagy defect in diabetic kidney disease
pmc-13661522.creator: Jia-ling Ji, Yun-yang Qiao, Jia-yue Sun, Ying Huo, Hui-min Shi, Gao-ting Qu, Shan-wen Li, Chan Huang, Yu Feng, Pei Zhang, Ling Ding, Zuo-lin Li, Ai-qing Zhang
pmc-13661522.description: Tubulointerstitial fibrosis (TIF) is a crucial pathological feature and inevitable consequence of progressive diabetic kidney disease (DKD). Transfer RNA-derived fragments (tRFs), a novel class of small non-coding RNA by cleavage of tRNAs, have recently attracted attention due to their functional significance in diverse biological processes. However, the role of tRFs in TIF is largely elusive.

pmc-13696775.creator: James A. Dolan, Hauke Riesch, Oana-Catalina Mihai
pmc-13696775.description: Over the past few decades, explicitly humorous or comedic science communication initiatives have become increasingly prominent.
